newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks soft, but Germany at record high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks soft, but Germany at record high.

text.p: European bourses were weaker at Tuesday's midsession after Wall Street snapped its three-day winning streak overnight but German shares bucked the trend to score a record high.
The dollar was about steady against the mark but came off its session high versus the yen as the mark weakened against sterling.
Sterling rose above 2.97 marks, its highest level since May 1991, near midmorning on hopes of an official British rate increase at the end of the Bank of England's two-day policy meeting on Thursday.
In metals, gold's slide to about 12-year lows slowed on physical demand overnight in Asia and the Middle East.
But traders said gold remained vulnerable to testing Monday's New York low of $314 per ounce and possibly, falling below $300 within a few months.
Precious metals "have been going sideways for so long that now, a trend has started. It will be very significant," said Fran Skelley, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
The dollar's firmness against the mark continued to lift German export shares, which led the 30-share DAX index up to an all-time high at the start of bourse trade.
Siemens AG was also among the winners, hitting a year high, in Frankfurt after Britain's General Electric Co Plc said it was reviewing its GPT telecoms joint venture with Siemens.
At 1055 GMT, Siemens was up 0.60 mark at 109.25, off its year high of 110.10 set early in the day.
Retailer Metro AG extended Monday's gains after Metro said on Monday it was talking with Dutch retailer SHV Holdings NV about taking over its cash and carry business.
At 1100 GMT, Metro shares were up 11.50 marks at 217.00, just off its year high of 219.00, set earlier in the day.
But Frankfurt's gains and the dollar's support for most European export shares failed to pull other European bourses higher.
Paris traders said the blue-chip CAC-40 index was choppy, pulled in opposite directions by the dollar's strength and Wall Street's volatile session overnight.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 37.32 points to end at 7,858.49 after racing to a record high of 7,951.45 at the open.

Alcatel Alsthom was among the biggest losers in Paris, shedding 1.64 percent to 778 French francs by 0900 GMT. Alcatel shares fell after General Electric Co Plc said it was in talks with the French company about the future of their GEC Alsthom joint venture.
Alcatel had no comment on the news.
London's FTSE-100 index held losses on interest rate and currency worries.
British government debt prices fell, pushing long-term interest rates higher, after Britain's June retail price index (RPI) rose 0.4 percent to exceed forecasts for a 0.2-percent increase.
The retail price jump reinforced ideas the Bank of England would raise official interest rates at least 25 basis points this week.

"The market is anxious about rates," a dealer said. "If (Bank of England) doesn't move, the market will go down. If rates are raised by a quarter (point), it will not be enough. And if they go by half a point, it (will) be perceived as a lack of confidence in (finance minister Gordon) Brown."

If interest rates rise, traders worried sterling would climb further and chip away more profits from British companies with substantial overseas exposure. A higher currency makes a firm's goods more expensive abroad.
According to a leading business survey, British engineering firms' second-quarter export orders fell to the lowest level in three years because of the pound's surge.
Against the dollar, the pound jumped above 1.69.
In the U.S., economic indicators due include weekly retail sales, the Richmond Federal Reserve's June survey of economic activity and May consumer credit.
CURRENCIES AT 1110 GMT
The dollar was at 112.63 yen and 1.7548 marks compared to 112.30 and 1.7458 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1110 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 32.1 points at 4,778.60.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 36.94 points at 4,009.78.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 8.28 points at 2,939.38.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $317.60 per ounce, down from $318.55 at London's close on Monday. Silver dropped to $4.25 in early London, down sharply from $4.45 at Monday's close in London.
